summary: Core engineer on a 15-service TypeScript monorepo for an AI-powered mortgage-lending platform, working across backend services, frontend, and infrastructure.
highlights: Designed and shipped production LLM pipelines for document data extraction, taking accuracy from 30% to 87% across the vendor-replacement experiments — at least as reliable as the incumbent OCR vendor, extending coverage to the roughly one-third of documents it only classified and never extracted, at about 3% of its cost.

Built the platform's communication infrastructure end to end: asynchronous email sync with durable retries and reconciliation, a new SMS channel behind a channel-agnostic abstraction, LLM-driven message classification, and loan matching over field-level-encrypted data — deliberately splitting the non-deterministic LLM classification from the deterministic rule set that decides where each message lands.

Turned agentic AI features into engineered systems: evaluation harnesses with LLM-as-judge scoring and human-graded ground truth, per-call cost tracing, version-controlled prompts, and an AI cost-reduction workstream.

Led a team evaluating vision-LLM document classification and extraction to replace the incumbent OCR vendor, personally designing and testing competing pipeline architectures — made 80+ page closing packets processable at a small fraction of the vendor's per-loan cost.

Built and evolved the flexible query-filtering layer behind the loan-application product: a reusable TypeScript filter library and query parser that compose MongoDB queries from user-facing filters — multi-value, related-entity, date-range, set/unset, and regex-escaped text-search operators — with tenant-scoped access for sensitive loan data.

Designed and delivered a monorepo-wide, agent-consumable documentation system with deterministic integrity gates in CI, alongside broad ownership of shared packages, public upload flows, user offboarding, observability, and production incident response.
